method: Use accepted physical serial replay costs and same-run Linux resume medians to compute the concurrency required for combined I+D background replay. Map 128/160/192 64-byte lines onto the measured 32-KiB, 64-set, 8-way I/D caches for a two-resident-context retention alternative. Address-history storage assumes 32 bits per remembered line including minimal metadata.

conclusion.linux_scheduler: At the 160-line middle point, combined I+D replay needs only 1.24x the measured serial replay rate (32.5 MB/s) to fit inside the existing 11.35k-cycle Linux resume interval.
conclusion.fast_hardware_handoff: A 5-11-cycle handoff cannot hide thousands of cycles of large replay; resident-context retention is required for immediate hot state, with a small signature useful only as a complement.
conclusion.capacity: For two resident contexts, 128/160/192 retained lines per context consume 4/5/6 of eight ways in each cache, leaving 4/3/2 ways unreserved. Ten simultaneous retained contexts cannot fit.
conclusion.hybrid: Use retention or partitioning for resident contexts, background replay for nonresident or ordinarily scheduled contexts, and the depth-two signature for first-touch assistance.

limits: This is an accounting model, not a concurrent replay or retention measurement.
Instruction and data replay may contend with scheduler traffic and with each other.
Strict 160-line retention is 2.5 ways per context and requires skewed/set-selective allocation rather than a uniform integer-way partition.
Refill-equivalent line counts are sizing guides, not exact unique line histories.
History storage excludes banking, ECC, generation tags, replacement state, and ports.
